TaskDescription: Each of two sessions, spaced at least one week apart, consisted of six blocks performed with eyes closed: resting state without meditation (5 min); pre-up meditation in the participant's standard Vipassana practice (5 min); meditation with a sustained attention passive oddball (SAPO) sequence of tones presented every 1 s, with standard tones (500 Hz, 80%), oddball tones (1000 Hz, 10%) and white-noise distractors (10%), which participants were instructed to ignore (35 min); an active oddball task in which participants pressed a button when they detected oddball tones (5 min); meditation without the SAPO sequence (SILENT, 35 min); and a cool-down meditation repeating the pre-up block (5 min). The two 35-minute meditation blocks were interchanged between a participant's two sessions. During the 35-minute blocks participants indicated the deepest level of meditation since their last report on a scale from 1 (shallow) to 5 (deepest), followed by a confidence rating on the same scale, using a clicker. In the emerge variant they reported spontaneously; in the probe variant they were prompted at random intervals of 3:00 to 3:50 min. Each participant completed each combination of variant and block type once over the two sessions. Meditation blocks were divided into sub-blocks of 100 to 120 s, each ending with a gong that served as a cue to refocus attention.
Instructions: Depth prompt: Please rate the depth of your meditation since your last response on a scale from 1-5. Confidence prompt: On a scale from 1-5, how confident are you in your response?
